summary: John Crook worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sherborne School, the University of Southampton, Jesus College, and under Sheng Yen. He held posts at the University of Bristol and Université Bouddhique Européenne, and founded the Western Chan Fellowship.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, John D. Dunne studied at Amherst College, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Harvard University. He held posts at Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Harvard, Antioch, Emory, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi from around 1976 to 1986, whom he succeeded, and served as Abbot at Zen Mountain Monastery from approximately 1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and received training under teachers Bernie Glassman and Taizan Maezumi.

John Dowson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. During his career, he held academic posts at University College London and served as Late Professor of Hindustani at Staff College, Camberley from around 1855 to 1877.

John E. Cort specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Harvard University, and served as a professor at Denison University starting around 1993.

John Faithfull Fleet worked in Indology and history and archaeology. After studying at University College London, he served in the Bombay Civil Service, the Indian Civil Service, and as Epigraphist for the Government of India from 1883 to 1886.

Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, John Gombojab Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University.

John H. Berthrong worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under graduate supervisor Alfonso Verdu until around 1979 and held a post at Boston University from roughly 1989 to 2019.

John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth College and held academic posts at Johns Hopkins University and Harvard University, serving as a professor at Harvard from around 1887 to 1908.
John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. In 1784, he served as secretary at the Asiatic Society, and in 1801, he held a post as professor at Fort William College.

John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies after studying at Scarborough College, the University of Edinburgh, and Oriel College. He held posts at Cornell, Princeton Theological Seminary, Cambridge, the University of Birmingham, and Claremont Graduate University.

John J. Holder specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Harry Krebs, held an associate professorship of philosophy at St. Norbert College beginning around 1989, and had a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford.

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, holding posts at Boston College, the Central Institute, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He completed an MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner, later holding posts at ANU, Griffith University, and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Bristol from around 2005 to 2011, and became a professor of Buddhist studies at Stanford University around 2011.
John Leyden was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Henry Thomas Colebrooke. From roughly 1806 to 1811, he served as assistant secretary and secretary at the Asiatic Society.
John Lockwood Kipling was a history and archaeology scholar who was educated at Woodhouse Grove School. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum from roughly 1875 to 1893.

John M. Koller works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, Kenneth K. Inada, and George T. Artola, and became a professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute around 1968.

John M. Rosenfield specialized in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Southern Methodist University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University, where he later served as a professor from around 1965 to 1995.
